=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:40 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The last autofix run added `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` to the transfer allowlist alongside the existing `gh_api_write_guard.py`. This lets the untrusted review editor modify and transfer a live PreToolUse safety hook to the host checkout.
  WHY: An editor-modified guard can weaken the merged-PR commit guard for future interactive sessions. However, the test at `test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:1007-1015` verifies this is gated: only the explicitly listed `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` is transferrable, and `unrelated.py` is rejected. The same safeguard already exists for `gh_api_write_guard.py`, which was added before this change. The risk is mitigated by the snapshot-transfer-refresh cycle: the editor runs in an isolated sandbox and cannot read the host's live guard, so it can only produce a plausible guard de novo, and the transfer-path test locks that only this one exact path is admitted.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py and workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: Root file (1474 lines) vs template file (1501 lines) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root and template copies of the merged-PR commit guard are out of sync. The root copy is missing the PR #6113 updates: redirect_target token handling in `_shell_segments_with_operators` at line 262-271 of the template, `|| exit` handling in `_guarded_git_invocations` at line 328-330, and `+=` assignment prefix matching at lines 351-357. The test `test_template_copies_are_identical` at `test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:998-1000` requires these files to be byte-identical and fails.
  WHY: The `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` CI job fails with 5 failures, which cascades to the aggregate `lint` check being red. The missing redirect_target logic can misparse push commands containing redirection operators, and the missing `+=` assignment matching can misparse guarded push commands prefixed with `+=` assignments. This is a pre-existing defect from the `[ai-merge-resolve]` merge commit, not introduced by the LAST RUN DIFF. The last autofix editor correctly identified this as unresolvable from its isolated checkout.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The CI `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` check must pass (the test `test_template_copies_are_identical` at `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:998-1000` needs `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` to be byte-identical).
  Expected change site: `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` — the root copy must be updated to match the template's 1501-line version that carries the PR #6113 fixes.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF does not touch `pr_merge_status_guard.py` at all. Neither does the PR DIFF — the original Phase 5c changes never modified this file. The divergence was introduced by the `[ai-merge-resolve]` merge commit that resolved conflicts incorrectly, keeping the stale root copy. The CI log_tail confirms `5 failed, 172 passed` on the hook tests, and the template parity test is one of the five failures.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py: lines 260-272, 339-345, 621-623 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The root hook .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (1474 lines) is out of sync with its template counterpart workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py (1501 lines). The root copy lacks updates from PR #6113 including redirect-target token handling in _shell_segments_with_operators(), \+?= variable assignment prefix matching in _guarded_git_invocations() and git_subcommands(), and cache re-check logic.
  WHY: In interactive sessions, guarded git commands preceded by += assignments (e.g., X+=1 git push) bypass the commit guard because the assignment is not recognized as a command prefix. In CI, tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py fails 5 tests (including test_template_copies_are_identical, which asserts that the root hook and template hook are byte-identical), causing the tests-hooks-and-orchestrator job and the aggregate lint check to fail with exit code 1.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: line 40 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: In the previous autofix run, .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py was added to allowed() in scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:40, alongside corresponding modifications in agents.md (line 72) and tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py (lines 8194, 8209, 8216, 8222).
  WHY: scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py enforces the sandbox isolation boundary, restricting which files the untrusted review editor running inside Docker can modify and transfer back to the host repository. .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py is an interactive Claude Code PreToolUse hook that executes implicitly on every host Bash tool call with full host authority. Permitting the untrusted editor container to transfer changes to this hook breaks the isolation boundary and allows untrusted code to weaken or disable host-level commit/push safety guards.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py: line 40 — `if name in (".github/ai/claude_engine.json", ".claude/hooks/gh_api_write_guard.py", ".claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py", "scripts/claude_settings.json.tmpl"):` | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The transfer allowlist now admits `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py`, the live `PreToolUse` Bash hook that enforces the merged-PR commit guard per CLAUDE.md §21. The transfer function (lines 151-189) writes editor-supplied bytes to the host file via tempfile + rename, gated only by a baseline fingerprint check (line 159). A malicious or buggy Claude editor session can therefore modify and ship a weakened guard to the host checkout; the host's later Bash tool calls run the modified hook with full tool-call authority. agents.md:72 documents the change as scoped to this hook plus the two other already-allowed `.claude/hooks/*` files, and `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:1014-1015` asserts the bounded allowlist, but the underlying host-write trust model is unchanged from the existing `gh_api_write_guard.py` allowance — and the merged-PR guard is a stronger safety check than the `gh` API guard it joins.
  WHY: A Claude editor that overwrites `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` with a stub that always returns exit 0 (allow) silently disables the merged-PR guard for the rest of the session; the next push to a branch whose PR has merged proceeds without the §21 block, stranding the work exactly as §21 exists to prevent.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: line 21138 — `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_RC=0` (inside the `for attempt in 1 2` loop of `invoke_review_blocked_judge`, introduced by this PR) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The other four Claude judge sites introduce their rc variables with `local` (line 6502 `local security_judge_rc=0`, line 8692 `local integration_judge_rc=0`, line 14735 `local stall_judge_rc=0`); the RB_JUDGE site does not. The variable leaks out of the loop and persists for the rest of the function. It does not cause an immediate runtime failure because line 21138 resets it on every iteration, but the inconsistency with the surrounding Phase 5c code is exactly the kind of latent scope bug that surfaces when a later caller shares the same name.
  WHY: A future edit that adds a sibling loop, sub-function, or refactor that also uses `RB_JUDGE_ENGINE_RC` will silently read a stale value across iterations; `set -u` does not help because the variable is always set, and the leak is in a function whose other globals (`RB_JUDGE_SUCCESS`, `RB_JUDGE_PROMPT_BYTES`, `RB_JUDGE_PROMPT_CHARS`) also lack `local` — so the inconsistency is broa
